reason: The PROBLEM verifies exactly; the PROPOSED FIX is wrong, and the rules say a correct problem with a wrong fix is refuted. Driven in chromium at 1280x900 and 1440x960 (v=light&state=full), both breaks are real and the seat's deltas are right even though its absolute page coordinates are ~10px off mine (constant offset, so the claim is unaffected): (a) the lead card's .t-num measures top 833.4 / bottom 868.8 while the other four sit at 838.6 / 873.9 — a 5.15px offset, not 6px, and the cause is exactly as stated (the lead's first slot is an 11px .t-label whose line box is 14.84px against the other four's 20px .glyph; 20 - 14.84 = 5.16); (b) a Range walk over the word blocks confirms 'have nobody's name on them' breaks after 'on' and 'are waiting on something else' after 'something', both orphaning one word, which moves those two meters from top 910.1 to 930.2 — a 20.14px stagger. At 390 all four wrap and meters agree within each row (1394.8 / 1567.4); at 768 none wrap and they agree (1276.1 / 1428.6). So it does break at exactly the two desk widths, nowhere else. Severity 'defect' is the right class and I confirm it: nothing is asserted untrue and every meter still fills to its true share, but the row's only comparable marks lose their common line in the one composition built for cross-comparison. Neither gate covers this — interaction-check.mjs asserts card COUNT, denominator arithmetic, that an unavailable card draws no meter, and skeleton-vs-real card height, never vertical agreement inside the row; audit.mjs walks the type ramp and leading ladder, not alignment. The fix is what fails. Rule two, '.kpi .meter, .kpi .na, .kpi .t-label:last-of-type { margin-top: auto; }', is broken on both of its non-meter selectors. `.kpi .na` matches `.t-num.na` — the em-dash NUMERAL of the unavailable card, not its 'Not available' label — so margin-top:auto shoves that numeral down: measured in state=partial at 1440, the overdue card's .t-num moves from top 838.6 to 846.9 under the seat's own CSS while the other four stay at 838.6. The fix written to give the row one baseline is the thing that breaks it, in the state where the honest-degradation contract is on show. And `.kpi .t-label:last-of-type` matches nothing at all: :last-of-type is by element type, every child is a <span>, and the last span in every card is the visually-hidden `.sr` line, so the 'Not available' label — the one element that rule was aimed at — is never pinned. It only appeared to land right in my test because the misplaced .na margin happened to push it there. Rule one is sound but half of it is dead weight: `.kpi .glyph { height: 20px; display: grid; place-items: center; }` restates what .glyph already declares at line 279.
sharpenedFix: Three lines, child-combinated so nothing reaches into the glyph's SVG or the .sr span, and with the unavailable card's label targeted by the class it actually carries: `.kpi > .glyph, .kpi.lead > .t-label { height: 20px; }` — the glyph is already 20px, so this only grows the lead's label box; `.kpi.lead > .t-label { display: flex; align-items: center; }` to centre the 14.84px line box in that 20px slot (flex, not grid, so the text is not blockified; no justify override is needed since the flex row already starts at the inline start); and `.kpi > .meter, .kpi > .t-label.dim { margin-top: auto; }` — `.t-label.dim` is the real class on the 'Not available' line, and dropping `.na` entirely leaves the numerals alone. Driven with exactly this CSS: at 1280 and 1440 all five .t-num tops become 838.6 and all four meter tops become 930.2; in state=partial the unavailable card's numeral stays at 838.6 and its 'Not available' label bottom-aligns to the meters' bottom edge (top 918.4, bottom 933.2 = meter bottom). At 390 and 768 the rules are no-ops on the meters, as they should be. Leave the words alone, as the seat says — do not chase the orphans with a nbsp or a shorter phrase; the phrasing is the product's voice and the fix should absorb the wrap, not fight it.
breaks: Three things to re-measure after it lands. (1) The lead card gains 5.2px of height wherever it is not row-stretched — measured 120.3 to 125.5 at both 390 and 768, where the 900px breakpoint gives it its own full-width row. It is unchanged at 1280/1440 because the wrapping cards still set the row height. Re-shoot light-full--390x844 and 768x1024 and their dark twins. (2) interaction-check.mjs asserts 'the skeleton card is the real card's height' within 8px against document.querySelector('.kpi'), which is the LEAD card. The skeleton is a clone of the real composition, so it moves with it — I drove state=loading at 390/768/1280 and the heights track the full state exactly (125.5 / 125.5 / 156.6) — but this is the one gate assertion the change can touch, so run interaction-check.mjs before calling it done. (3) The visual cost is a whitespace trade, not a free win: with meters pinned, the two one-line cards now carry a ~20px gap between their word block and their meter while the two wrapping cards keep the 8px --gap-tight. That is the right trade — the meters are the comparable marks and the gap is above them, not between them — but it should be eyeballed in the frame rather than assumed, and it means the row now reads as four cards of equal footer rather than four cards of equal text block. Also re-run audit.mjs: the change adds height and display to elements the type ramp walks, and while it does not touch font-size or line-height, the leading-ladder check reads computed style on exactly these nodes.
